problem: All VLN-CE benchmarks and methods assume the language instruction is correct. Real human instructions contain mistakes (swapped directions, confused rooms or objects), and no benchmark or task existed to measure how robust agents are to such errors or to detect and locate them.
motivation: Humans give instructions from imperfect memory. In a pilot study, SOTA VLN-CE agents lost up to 25% Success Rate when an instruction contained up to three injected errors. Yet a trajectory often still holds enough evidence to notice the mismatch; for example, the 'big clock' mentioned in the instruction is never seen. So the authors argue that detecting and localizing instruction errors is a necessary intermediate step toward error-aware VLN.
key_idea: Build R2RIE-CE by injecting human-plausible Direction, Room and Object errors into R2R-CE val-unseen instructions. Then train a cross-modal transformer that fuses the instruction with the visual trajectory of a frozen VLN policy (BEVBert) to decide whether the instruction is erroneous and which tokens are wrong.
insight: (1) Instruction errors clearly hurt a frozen SOTA policy (BEVBert). Direction errors hurt far more than object or room errors (ΔSR -18.64 vs -8.47 and -6.66). This reverses prior discrete-VLN findings; the authors attribute the difference to nav-graph implicit assumptions. (2) Simply checking whether instruction nouns are grounded in CLIP detections along the path (the CLIP-based baseline) works somewhat for room and object errors (AUC 0.57-0.64) but is at chance on direction errors (0.50). A learned instruction–trajectory compatibility model does much better (avg AUC 0.79), although direction errors remain hard (0.58). (3) Localization reaches a mean token distance of 7.71, roughly the length of one sub-sentence. The detector also surfaced real annotation errors in R2R-CE and RxR-CE val sets. No component ablations are reported.
method: R2RIE-CE benchmark construction: filter R2R-CE val-unseen episodes (minimum length τ words, must contain the relevant word types). Create a perturbed copy of each by swapping words: directions to antonyms (left/right, go up/go down, into/out of, forward/backward, inside/outside, etc.); objects to co-occurring object classes; rooms to adjacent rooms (ConceptNet plus manual curation). Five variants: Direction, Room, Object, Room&Object (2 errors), All (3 errors). Error positions and types are stored as metadata.
Task definition: detection d_π maps (instruction, observations of policy π) to True/False; localization l_π maps them to a set of erroneous word indices.

IEDL feature inputs: BEVBert serves as the frozen policy π and produces a trajectory. Each chosen node's panorama is encoded with CLIP ViT-B/16 plus a HAMT-style panoramic encoder (D=768) and given sine/cosine positional encoding. A learnable [CLS] token is prepended. The instruction is BERT-embedded and padded to W=80 tokens.
Cross-modal transformer: k=4 LXMERT-like layers without the bidirectional part. Each layer runs cross-attention (trajectory as query, instruction as key/value), then self-attention, then an FFN.

Two heads on [CLS] (MLP-ReLU-LayerNorm-MLP): a detection head gives a sigmoid alignment score trained with BCE; a localization head outputs W logits trained with CE, averaged over the E errors. Loss is L = λ1·L_d + λ2/E·ΣL_l with λ1=λ2=1, AdamW, up to 9k iterations.

Training protocol: train on R2R-CE train with All-type errors injected without common-sense priors (random swaps). Select the checkpoint by AUC on the val-unseen All benchmark with common sense. Use that single model for all benchmarks.
Dataset auditing use: threshold the alignment score (τ_a=0.99) on the original R2R-CE and RxR-CE val sets to flag suspicious episodes for manual inspection.

setting.backbone: Frozen BEVBert VLN-CE policy (generates trajectories; its CLIP ViT-B/16 + panoramic-encoder features are reused) + BERT text embeddings + 4-layer cross-modal transformer trained for error detection/localization
setting.training_data: R2R-CE train split with artificially injected All-type instruction errors (random swaps, no common-sense priors), paired with trajectories from the frozen BEVBert policy
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (via BEVBert); detector consumes per-step panoramic visual embeddings of the executed trajectory + the full instruction
setting.action_space: detector outputs binary error flag + token-index localization; underlying policy acts in VLN-CE low-level space (FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15° / STOP) via BEVBert waypoints
setting.privileged: none (post-hoc on the policy's own executed trajectory)

numbers.eval_set_note: R2RIE-CE benchmark built from filtered R2R-CE val-unseen episodes: Direction 3218, Room 2064, Object 3162, Room&Object 1734, All 1586 episodes (correct + perturbed, 50/50)
numbers.extra: single model trained on R2R-CE train with All-type errors (no common sense); checkpoint selected on val-unseen All (with common sense) benchmark, i.e. same split as evaluation; Room/Object/Room&Object/All test sets use common-sense error priors
numbers.evidence: Table 'Results of our proposed ... method on our proposed benchmark' (table:task_1), columns for our method; Avg. row 0.79 / 7.71

numbers_note: The paper's only quantitative results are for the new R2RIE-CE detection/localization task (AUC is a 0-1 score, ATD is in tokens). The BEVBert policy SR/SPL on the error sets (e.g. Direction SR 0.53, ΔSR -18.64; All SR 0.52, ΔSR -30.64) are frozen-baseline numbers and are not listed in 'numbers'. The SR drops for other VLN-CE methods (up to -25%) appear only in Fig. 2. The R2R-CE and RxR-CE annotation-error findings are counts, not metrics.
results: Injecting errors reduces BEVBert's SR on R2R-CE val-unseen by 6.66% (Room) up to 30.64% (All), with Direction errors the most harmful single type (-18.64%). IEDL reaches average AUC 0.79 and ATD 7.71, against Random (0.50 / 11.26) and a training-free CLIP-grounding baseline (0.59 / 9.22). It is best on every error type for AUC and on every type except Object for ATD, peaking at AUC 0.94 on All. Run as a filter on the original data, it flagged 25 of 1839 R2R-CE val-unseen episodes, of which 8 were confirmed wrong annotations. Applied to ETPNav on RxR-CE without retraining, it flagged 118 of 3669 episodes, of which 10 were confirmed erroneous.
limitations: Errors are synthetic single-word swaps (antonyms, co-occurring objects, adjacent rooms), not real human-produced erroneous instructions. Detection is offline, after the full trajectory is executed. The method does not improve navigation itself; error-aware policies are left to future work.
Direction errors, the most harmful type, remain poorly detected (AUC 0.58). There are no ablations of architecture or input components.

Checkpoint selection uses the val-unseen All benchmark, the same split used for evaluation, so the All AUC of 0.94 is optimistic. The detector is tied to BEVBert trajectories and features; generalization to ETPNav/RxR-CE is shown only qualitatively.
compares_to: CLIP-based zero-shot grounding baseline (POS-tagged room/object tokens checked against CLIP top-k labels)
